content.json:
# Azure AI estate - issues and model retirement

Fleet-wide view of **Azure OpenAI**, **Microsoft Foundry**, **Foundry projects** and
**AI Hub / AI Project** workspaces: security posture, network exposure, model
deployments, model retirement dates and AI service retirement advisories.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.label: Subscriptions
parameters.query:
resourcecontainers
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
| where properties.state =~ 'Enabled'
| project value = id, label = name, selected = true
| order by label asc
parameters.description: Subscriptions to scan for AI resources.

parameters.name: ResourceGroups
parameters.label: Resource groups
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
   or type =~ 'microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces'
| summarize Items = count() by resourceGroup
| project value = resourceGroup, label = strcat(resourceGroup, ' (', Items, ')'), selected = false
| order by label asc

parameters.name: ModelAccounts
parameters.label: Model account
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| where kind in~ ('OpenAI','AIServices')
| extend kindRank = iff(kind =~ 'OpenAI', 0, 1)
| order by kindRank asc, name asc
| extend rn = row_number()
| project value = id, label = strcat(name, '  [', kind, ']'), selected = (rn == 1)
parameters.description: Account whose model deployments are listed. Set by clicking a row in the account grid on the Model deployments tab.

parameters.name: AccountRegion
parameters.label: Account region
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| where tolower(id) == tolower('{ModelAccounts}')
| project value = location, label = location, selected = true
parameters.description: Region of the selected model account, used to read the matching model catalog.

parameters.name: AccountSubscription
parameters.label: Account subscription
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| where tolower(id) == tolower('{ModelAccounts}')
| project value = subscriptionId, label = subscriptionId, selected = true
parameters.description: Subscription of the selected model account.

parameters.name: AccountKind
parameters.label: Account kind
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| where tolower(id) == tolower('{ModelAccounts}')
| project value = tostring(kind), label = tostring(kind), selected = true
parameters.description: Kind of the selected account, used to de-duplicate the model catalog.

## Azure AI estate - issue overview

Covers **Azure OpenAI**, **Microsoft Foundry (AI Services)**, **Foundry projects**,
and **AI Hub / AI Project** workspaces across every selected subscription.

Account and workspace findings come from **Azure Resource Graph**. Model
deployments are *not* indexed by Resource Graph at all, so the **Model deployments**
tab reads them from the Azure Resource Manager control plane instead. See
**About the data** for the measured details.

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| extend acctKind   = tostring(kind)
| extend isModelHost = (acctKind in~ ('OpenAI','AIServices'))
| extend skuName    = tostring(sku.name)
| extend identityType = tostring(identity.type)
| extend pna        = tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess)
| extend localAuthDisabled = tobool(properties.disableLocalAuth)
| extend subdomain  = tostring(properties.customSubDomainName)
| extend restrictOutbound = tobool(properties.restrictOutboundNetworkAccess)
| extend netDefault = tostring(properties.networkAcls.defaultAction)
| extend ipRuleCount = toint(array_length(todynamic(properties.networkAcls.ipRules)))
| extend vnetRuleCount = toint(array_length(todynamic(properties.networkAcls.virtualNetworkRules)))
| extend cmkSource  = tostring(properties.encryption.keySource)
| extend allowProjectMgmt = tobool(properties.allowProjectManagement)
| extend state      = tostring(properties.provisioningState)
| extend created    = todatetime(properties.dateCreated)
| extend endpoint   = tostring(properties.endpoint)
| extend isMigrated = tobool(properties.isMigrated)
| extend peCount    = toint(array_length(todynamic(properties.privateEndpointConnections)))
| extend KindLabel  = case(
      acctKind =~ 'OpenAI',     'Azure OpenAI',
      acctKind =~ 'AIServices', 'Microsoft Foundry (AI Services)',
      acctKind =~ 'CognitiveServices', 'Cognitive Services (multi-service)',
      acctKind)
| extend IssueList = array_concat(
    iff(localAuthDisabled != true,                      pack_array('API key (local) auth enabled - prefer Entra ID'), dynamic([])),
    iff(pna =~ 'Enabled' and peCount == 0,              pack_array('Public network access with no private endpoint'), dynamic([])),
    iff(pna =~ 'Enabled' and netDefault !~ 'Deny',      pack_array('Network ACLs allow all traffic'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isempty(identityType) or identityType =~ 'None', pack_array('No managed identity'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isModelHost and isempty(subdomain),             pack_array('No custom subdomain - Entra ID auth unavailable'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isempty(cmkSource) or cmkSource =~ 'Microsoft.CognitiveServices', pack_array('Microsoft-managed keys (no CMK)'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isModelHost and restrictOutbound != true,       pack_array('Outbound network access unrestricted'), dynamic([])),
    iff(state !~ 'Succeeded',                           pack_array(strcat('Provisioning state: ', state)), dynamic([]))
  )
| extend IssueCount = array_length(IssueList)
| extend Issues     = strcat_array(IssueList, ' | ')
| extend Severity = case(
      IssueCount >= 6, 'Critical',
      IssueCount >= 4, 'High',
      IssueCount >= 2, 'Medium',
      IssueCount >= 1, 'Low',
                       'Healthy')
| extend SeverityRank = case(Severity == 'Critical', 0, Severity == 'High', 1, Severity == 'Medium', 2, Severity == 'Low', 3, 4)
| summarize
    ModelHosts  = countif(isModelHost),
    OpenAIAcct  = countif(acctKind =~ 'OpenAI'),
    FoundryAcct = countif(acctKind =~ 'AIServices'),
    OtherAI     = countif(isModelHost == false),
    AtRisk      = countif(IssueCount > 0),
    CritHigh    = countif(Severity in ('Critical','High')),
    KeyAuth     = countif(localAuthDisabled != true),
    OpenNet     = countif(pna =~ 'Enabled' and peCount == 0)
| extend Tiles = pack_array(
    pack('Metric', 'Model-hosting accounts',   'Value', ModelHosts,  'Rank', 1),
    pack('Metric', 'Azure OpenAI',             'Value', OpenAIAcct,  'Rank', 2),
    pack('Metric', 'Microsoft Foundry',        'Value', FoundryAcct, 'Rank', 3),
    pack('Metric', 'Other AI services',        'Value', OtherAI,     'Rank', 4),
    pack('Metric', 'Accounts with findings',   'Value', AtRisk,      'Rank', 5),
    pack('Metric', 'Critical or high',         'Value', CritHigh,    'Rank', 6),
    pack('Metric', 'API key auth enabled',     'Value', KeyAuth,     'Rank', 7),
    pack('Metric', 'Public, no private endpoint', 'Value', OpenNet,  'Rank', 8))
| mv-expand Tiles
| project Metric = tostring(Tiles.Metric), Value = toint(Tiles.Value), Rank = toint(Tiles.Rank)
| order by Rank asc
content.title: AI estate summary

content.json:
## Model deployments

**Azure Resource Graph cannot see model deployments.** The type
`microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/deployments` returns zero rows - this was
measured against live deployments, not assumed.

This tab uses the **Azure Resource Manager** control plane, which returns deployments
for **one account at a time**. Click a row in the account list below to switch
accounts, or use the **Model account** parameter at the top.

> **Seeing an empty grid?** That usually means the selected account genuinely hosts
> no models. **Microsoft Foundry (AI Services)** accounts are frequently used for
> Document Intelligence, Speech or Vision rather than model hosting, so they
> legitimately have zero deployments. Azure OpenAI accounts are therefore listed and
> selected first. Try another account.

> **Why not all accounts at once?** Workbook ARM queries only accept a single Azure
> *resource* path - a tenant-level `POST /batch` is rejected with
> *"Path must be for an Azure Resource"*, and a multi-value parameter is joined
> into one malformed path rather than fanned out. Both were tested against the
> live portal. The workbook therefore shows deployments for one selected account
> at a time.

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| where kind in~ ('OpenAI','AIServices')
| extend kindRank = iff(kind =~ 'OpenAI', 0, 1)
| project
    Account = name,
    Kind = iff(kind =~ 'OpenAI', 'Azure OpenAI', 'Microsoft Foundry (AI Services)'),
    ['Resource group'] = resourceGroup,
    Region = location,
    SKU = tostring(sku.name),
    State = tostring(properties.provisioningState),
    Endpoint = tostring(properties.endpoint),
    kindRank,
    ResourceId = id
| order by kindRank asc, Account asc
| project-away kindRank
content.title: Model-hosting accounts (click a row to load its deployments)

content.json:
### Deployments for the selected account

* **Version upgrade policy** - `NoAutoUpgrade` means the deployment will **not**
  move off a retiring model version on its own. Those are your migration risks.
  `OnceCurrentVersionExpired` auto-upgrades only at expiry;
  `OnceNewDefaultVersionAvailable` tracks the current default.
* **Content filter** - a deployment with no RAI policy is unfiltered.
* **SKU** - `Standard` / `GlobalStandard` are pay-as-you-go; `ProvisionedManaged` is reserved capacity.

This grid is the authoritative response from the selected account's
`/deployments` endpoint: **one row per actual deployment**. It deliberately does not
merge the model catalog into this table. Azure Workbooks supports only one join key,
and composite JSONPath keys can evaluate empty in some portal runtimes, producing a
cross join where every deployment is repeated for every catalog model.

Use **Model retirement** for the live regional lifecycle calendar. Match the
deployment's model and version to the corresponding catalog row.

**Two things to expect:**

* An empty grid means the selected account has no model deployments. This is normal
  for AI Services accounts used for Document Intelligence, Speech, or Vision.
* **Tick exactly one account.** Azure Workbooks send an ARM query to **one Azure
  resource path at a time** - `GET` and `GETARRAY` were both tested and each joins
  multiple selected values into a single malformed path, and there is no
  subscription-wide deployments API. Selecting several accounts will error.

content.json:
## Model retirement calendar

Live retirement dates straight from the Azure model catalog, via the Resource
Manager control plane. Nothing here is hard-coded, so the dates stay correct as
Microsoft updates them.

The catalog shown is for the **region, subscription and account kind of the account
currently selected on the Model deployments tab** - pick a different account there to
see a different catalog.

> **Why the kind filter matters.** Azure returns the catalog once **per account kind**,
> so the same model is listed several times - `gpt-4.1` appears once as `OpenAI` and
> again as `AIServices` with identical dates. Unfiltered, a single region returned
> **167 duplicated rows**. This grid is filtered to the selected account's kind, which
> removes the duplicates and shows exactly the models **that account** can run.

**How to use this tab**

1. Note each model + version you actually run on the **Model deployments** tab.
2. Find that model + version below to get its **Inference retirement** date.
3. Prioritise any deployment whose **Version upgrade policy** is `NoAutoUpgrade` -
   those will not migrate themselves.

**Lifecycle meanings**

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GenerallyAvailable` | Supported for production |
| `Preview` | Not for production; can be retired at short notice |
| `Deprecating` | Retirement scheduled - **new deployments are already blocked** |
| `Deprecated` | Retired - existing deployments stop serving traffic |

Azure blocks new deployments of deprecating/deprecated versions, but **existing
deployments keep running until the retirement date and then fail**. That gap is
exactly what this tab is for.

## Account security and network posture

Every column is backed by a property that Resource Graph genuinely populates for
`microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts`. This was confirmed by setting each field
through ARM and re-reading it in Resource Graph - so a blank value means
*not configured*, never *not indexed*.

content.json:
## Microsoft Foundry projects

Foundry projects (`microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/projects`) **are** indexed
by Resource Graph. Each project inherits its parent Foundry account's
authentication and network configuration, so the parent's posture is joined in below.

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/projects'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| summarize Projects = count(), Accounts = dcount(tostring(split(name, '/')[0]))
| extend Tiles = pack_array(
    pack('Metric', 'Foundry projects', 'Value', Projects, 'Rank', 1),
    pack('Metric', 'Foundry accounts hosting projects', 'Value', Accounts, 'Rank', 2))
| mv-expand Tiles
| project Metric = tostring(Tiles.Metric), Value = toint(Tiles.Value), Rank = toint(Tiles.Rank)
| order by Rank asc
content.title: Foundry project summary

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/projects'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| extend accountName = tostring(split(name, '/')[0])
| extend projectName = tostring(split(name, '/')[-1])
| extend parentId = tolower(substring(id, 0, indexof(id, '/projects/')))
| join kind=leftouter (
    resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
    | project parentId = tolower(id), parentPna = tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess),
              parentLocalAuth = tobool(properties.disableLocalAuth)
  ) on parentId
| project
    Project = projectName,
    ['Foundry account'] = accountName,
    ['Resource group'] = resourceGroup,
    Region = location,
    ['Display name'] = tostring(properties.displayName),
    ['Is default'] = iff(tobool(properties.isDefault) == true, 'Yes', 'No'),
    ['Managed identity'] = iff(isempty(tostring(identity.type)) or tostring(identity.type) =~ 'None', 'None', tostring(identity.type)),
    State = tostring(properties.provisioningState),
    ['Parent public access'] = iff(isempty(parentPna), 'Unknown', parentPna),
    ['Parent Entra ID only'] = case(isnull(parentLocalAuth), 'Unknown', parentLocalAuth == true, 'Yes', 'No'),
    ResourceId = id
| order by ['Foundry account'] asc, Project asc
content.title: Foundry projects

content.json:
## AI Hub, AI Project and Azure ML workspaces

Covers `microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces` of every kind - **Hub**,
**Project**, plain **Azure ML workspace** and **feature store**. AI Projects are
matched back to their parent hub.

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces'
| extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
| extend wsKind   = tostring(kind)
| extend hubId    = tostring(properties.hubResourceId)
| extend pna      = tostring(properties.publicNetworkAccess)
| extend isolation = tostring(properties.managedNetwork.isolationMode)
| extend authMode = tostring(properties.systemDatastoresAuthMode)
| extend cmkEnabled = tobool(properties.enableServiceSideCMKEncryption)
| extend hbi      = tobool(properties.hbiWorkspace)
| extend softDelete = tobool(properties.softDeleteEnabled)
| extend privateLinks = toint(properties.privateLinkCount)
| extend v1Legacy = tobool(properties.v1LegacyMode)
| extend dataIsolation = tobool(properties.enableDataIsolation)
| extend identityType = tostring(identity.type)
| extend state    = tostring(properties.provisioningState)
| extend friendly = tostring(properties.friendlyName)
| extend created  = todatetime(properties.creationTime)
| extend storageId = tostring(properties.storageAccount)
| extend kvId     = tostring(properties.keyVault)
| extend KindLabel = case(
      wsKind =~ 'Hub',     'AI Hub',
      wsKind =~ 'Project', 'AI Project',
      wsKind =~ 'Default', 'Azure ML workspace',
      wsKind =~ 'FeatureStore', 'Feature store',
      iff(isempty(wsKind), 'Azure ML workspace', wsKind))
| extend IssueList = array_concat(
    iff(pna =~ 'Enabled' and privateLinks == 0,   pack_array('Public network access with no private link'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isolation =~ 'Disabled',                  pack_array('Managed VNet isolation disabled'), dynamic([])),
    iff(authMode =~ 'accesskey',                  pack_array('Datastores use access keys - prefer identity'), dynamic([])),
    iff(cmkEnabled != true,                       pack_array('No customer-managed key encryption'), dynamic([])),
    iff(isempty(identityType) or identityType =~ 'None', pack_array('No managed identity'), dynamic([])),
    iff(softDelete != true,                       pack_array('Soft delete not enabled'), dynamic([])),
    iff(v1Legacy == true,                         pack_array('v1 legacy mode enabled'), dynamic([])),
    iff(wsKind =~ 'Project' and isempty(hubId),   pack_array('Project not linked to a hub'), dynamic([])),
    iff(state !~ 'Succeeded',                     pack_array(strcat('Provisioning state: ', state)), dynamic([]))
  )
| extend IssueCount = array_length(IssueList)
| extend Issues     = strcat_array(IssueList, ' | ')
| extend Severity = case(
      IssueCount >= 6, 'Critical',
      IssueCount >= 4, 'High',
      IssueCount >= 2, 'Medium',
      IssueCount >= 1, 'Low',
                       'Healthy')
| extend SeverityRank = case(Severity == 'Critical', 0, Severity == 'High', 1, Severity == 'Medium', 2, Severity == 'Low', 3, 4)
| summarize
    Hubs = countif(wsKind =~ 'Hub'),
    Projects = countif(wsKind =~ 'Project'),
    Other = countif(wsKind !~ 'Hub' and wsKind !~ 'Project'),
    AtRisk = countif(IssueCount > 0),
    NoIsolation = countif(isolation =~ 'Disabled'),
    KeyDatastores = countif(authMode =~ 'accesskey')
| extend Tiles = pack_array(
    pack('Metric', 'AI Hubs',                  'Value', Hubs,          'Rank', 1),
    pack('Metric', 'AI Projects',              'Value', Projects,      'Rank', 2),
    pack('Metric', 'Other ML workspaces',      'Value', Other,         'Rank', 3),
    pack('Metric', 'Workspaces with findings', 'Value', AtRisk,        'Rank', 4),
    pack('Metric', 'Managed VNet disabled',    'Value', NoIsolation,   'Rank', 5),
    pack('Metric', 'Datastores using keys',    'Value', KeyDatastores, 'Rank', 6))
| mv-expand Tiles
| project Metric = tostring(Tiles.Metric), Value = toint(Tiles.Value), Rank = toint(Tiles.Rank)
| order by Rank asc
content.title: Workspace summary

content.json:
## Azure service retirements

This tab shows two independent retirement sources in separate grids. The rows are not
joined or merged:

* **Service Health retirements** are advisories retained for the selected
  subscriptions. They include both upcoming deadlines and past-due retirements that
  might still require customer action, with tracking ID, status, summary, and date.
* **Advisor retirements** are the Microsoft-published metadata catalog for AI, Data,
  Network, and Infrastructure services since 2024, including both elapsed and future
  dates. The **# Resources** column counts matching Advisor recommendations in the
  selected subscription/resource-group scope. Select a row to inspect those resources
  in the grid below.

Service Health and Advisor remain separate sources. The Advisor count and resource
details are derived only from `advisorresources` recommendation records.

content.query:
servicehealthresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resourcehealth/events'
| extend
    eventType = tostring(properties.EventType),
    eventSubType = tostring(properties.EventSubType)
| where eventType == 'HealthAdvisory' and eventSubType == 'Retirement'
| extend
    status = tostring(properties.Status),
    retirementTitle = tostring(properties.Title),
    trackingId = tostring(properties.TrackingId),
    retirementSummary = tostring(properties.Summary),
    retirementDate = todatetime(tolong(properties.ImpactMitigationTime))
| where isnotnull(retirementDate)
| extend retirementText = tolower(strcat(retirementTitle, ' ', retirementSummary))
| where retirementText contains 'azure ai'
    or retirementText contains 'microsoft foundry'
    or retirementText contains 'azure openai'
    or retirementText contains 'machine learning'
    or retirementText contains 'cognitive services'
    or retirementText contains 'ai services'
    or retirementText contains 'prompt flow'
    or retirementText contains 'model inference'
    or retirementText contains 'agent service'
    or retirementText contains 'qnamaker'
    or retirementText contains 'qna maker'
    or retirementText contains 'language understanding'
    or retirementText contains 'computer vision'
    or retirementText contains 'custom vision'
    or retirementText contains 'form recognizer'
    or retirementText contains 'document intelligence'
    or retirementText contains 'speech service'
    or retirementText contains 'content moderator'
    or retirementText contains 'anomaly detector'
    or retirementText contains 'personalizer'
    or retirementText contains 'metrics advisor'
    or retirementText contains 'azure bot'
    or retirementText contains 'cognitive search'
    or retirementText contains 'azure ai search'
| extend
    cleanSummary = trim(' ', replace_regex(retirementSummary, '<[^>]+>', ' ')),
    deadlineStatus = iff(retirementDate < now(), 'Past due', 'Upcoming')
| project
    ['Tracking ID'] = trackingId,
    Subscription = subscriptionId,
    Status = status,
    ['Deadline status'] = deadlineStatus,
    Retirement = retirementTitle,
    Summary = cleanSummary,
    ['Retirement date'] = retirementDate
| order by ['Retirement date'] asc
content.title: Service Health retirements: past due and upcoming

| where iff(strlen(name) == 36, properties.lastUpdated > ago(1d), properties.platformState == 'New')
| where isempty(properties.tracked)
| extend
    ResourceId = tolower(tostring(properties.resourceMetadata.resourceId)),
    ServiceID = tostring(properties.recommendationTypeId)
| where isnotempty(ResourceId) and isnotempty(ServiceID)
| join kind=inner (
    resources
    | extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
    | project ResourceId = tolower(id)

content.query:
advisorresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.advisor/recommendations'
| where iff(strlen(name) == 36, properties.lastUpdated > ago(1d), properties.platformState == 'New')
| where isempty(properties.tracked)
| extend
    ResourceId = tolower(tostring(properties.resourceMetadata.resourceId)),
    ServiceID = tostring(properties.recommendationTypeId),
    RecommendationState = tostring(properties.platformState)
| where isnotempty(ResourceId)
    and isnotempty(ServiceID)
    and ServiceID == '{SelectedRetirementServiceId}'
| join kind=inner (
    resources
    | extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
    | project
        ResourceId = tolower(id),
        Resource = name,
        ['Resource group'] = resourceGroup,
        Location = location,
        ['Resource type'] = type,
        Subscription = subscriptionId,
        Tags = tostring(tags)
  ) on ResourceId
| project
    Resource,
    ['Resource group'],
    ['Resource type'],
    Location,
    Subscription,
    ['Recommendation state'] = RecommendationState,
    ResourceId,
    Tags
| distinct Resource, ['Resource group'], ['Resource type'], Location, Subscription, ['Recommendation state'], ResourceId, Tags
| order by Resource asc

## Azure Advisor and Resource Health

Reads the `advisorresources` and `healthresources` tables for AI accounts and ML
workspaces. Empty panels mean no recommendations or health events exist for the
selected resources - a valid healthy result, not an error.

content.query:
advisorresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.advisor/recommendations'
| extend targetId = tolower(tostring(properties.resourceMetadata.resourceId))
| join kind=inner (
    resources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
       or type =~ 'microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces'
    | extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
    | project targetId = tolower(id), rName = name, rRg = resourceGroup, rType = type
  ) on targetId
| project
    Resource = rName,
    ['Resource group'] = rRg,
    Category = tostring(properties.category),
    Impact = tostring(properties.impact),
    Problem = tostring(properties.shortDescription.problem),
    Solution = tostring(properties.shortDescription.solution),
    ResourceId = targetId
| order by Impact asc, Resource asc
content.title: Advisor recommendations

content.query:
healthresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resourcehealth/availabilitystatuses'
| extend targetId = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| join kind=inner (
    resources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts'
       or type =~ 'microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces'
    | extend _rgs = dynamic([{ResourceGroups}])
| where array_length(_rgs) == 0 or set_has_element(_rgs, '*') or set_has_element(_rgs, resourceGroup)
    | project targetId = tolower(id), rName = name, rRg = resourceGroup
  ) on targetId
| project
    Resource = rName,
    ['Resource group'] = rRg,
    Availability = tostring(properties.availabilityState),
    Summary = tostring(properties.summary),
    ['Since'] = todatetime(properties.occuredTime),
    ResourceId = targetId
| order by Availability asc

content.json:
## About the data in this workbook

This workbook mixes two data sources on purpose, because neither one alone can
cover an Azure AI estate.

### What Azure Resource Graph can and cannot see

Measured against live fixtures, not assumed from ARM template documentation:

| Resource type | Indexed in Resource Graph? |
| --- | --- |
| `microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts` | **Yes** - fully, and verified to match the ARM control plane exactly |
| `microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/projects` (Foundry projects) | **Yes** |
| `microsoft.machinelearningservices/workspaces` (Hub / Project / ML) | **Yes** - rich properties |
| `microsoft.cognitiveservices/accounts/deployments` (**model deployments**) | **No - zero rows. Not indexed at all.** |

For accounts, each of `identity.type`, `disableLocalAuth`, `publicNetworkAccess`,
`restrictOutboundNetworkAccess`, `networkAcls.defaultAction`, `networkAcls.ipRules`,
`allowProjectManagement` and `customSubDomainName` was **set through ARM and then
re-read in Resource Graph** to confirm it round-trips. A blank value therefore means
*not configured*, never *not indexed*.

### How model data is retrieved

Because model deployments are invisible to Resource Graph:

1. A Resource Graph query lists every in-scope Azure OpenAI / Foundry account.
2. The Model deployments tab reads the selected account's ARM `/deployments`
   endpoint directly, with one grid row per returned deployment.
3. The Model retirement tab reads the regional model catalog
   (`.../locations/{region}/models`) for live retirement dates and lifecycle status.

The deployments grid is deliberately not merged with the catalog: Workbooks exposes
only one join-column pair, and a composite JSONPath key can evaluate empty in some
portal runtimes, turning the merge into a deployment-by-catalog cross join.
Retirement dates are never hard-coded - they come from the catalog at query time.

### How service retirement data is retrieved

The **Service retirements** tab keeps Service Health and Advisor as independent
sources:

1. `ServiceHealthResources` from Azure Resource Graph for subscription-specific
   Health Advisory retirement events retained by Azure, including elapsed deadlines.
2. `providers/Microsoft.Advisor/metadata` from the ARM control plane for Microsoft's
   published Service Upgrade and Retirement metadata catalog from 2024 onward,
   including elapsed and future dates.

The Service Health grid is filtered to AI-related retirement titles and summaries.
The Advisor summary covers AI, Data, Network, and Infrastructure metadata. Within
the Advisor section only, direct recommendation IDs are left-joined to resource
counts from `advisorresources`; row selection filters a separate affected-resources
grid below. Advisor metadata is a global planning catalog and does not by itself
prove that a service is deployed in the selected scope.

### Findings

**Accounts** - API key auth enabled instead of Entra ID only; public network access
with no private endpoint; network ACLs allowing all traffic; no managed identity;
no custom subdomain (which blocks Entra ID auth); Microsoft-managed keys instead of
CMK; unrestricted outbound access; failed provisioning.

**Workspaces** - public access with no private link; managed VNet isolation disabled;
datastores using access keys instead of identity; no CMK; no managed identity; soft
delete off; v1 legacy mode; project not linked to a hub; failed provisioning.

| Severity | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Critical | 6 or more findings |
| High | 4-5 findings |
| Medium | 2-3 findings |
| Low | 1 finding |
| Healthy | No findings |

which tab and which account or deployment is involved, and the fix will be turned
around quickly.
